notes: East Devon operates mandatory HMO licensing only. There is no selective licensing and no additional HMO licensing scheme. The council's HMO fee page lists mandatory licence fees only (£600 up to 5 occupants, £800 for 6 or more).
research: The HMO licensing page describes only the mandatory regime: 'properties occupied by five or more people making up two or more households', with the standard s.254 tests and the usual exemptions (s.257 HMOs, educational institutions, RSLs, religious communities). The application form page is titled 'Mandatory HMO Licence Application Form' and refers to the government 'extending the mandatory HMO licensing scheme', i.e. the 1 October 2018 national extension, not a local designation. FEE CORROBORATION: the HMO application fee page lists new licence fees as 'Up to 5 occupants = £600, 6 or more occupants = £800'. There is no fee line for a selective or additional licence anywhere in East Devon's published housing or environmental health fee schedules; the Environmental Health Licensing Fees page covers only animal licensing, skin piercing, export certificates and scrap metal. Council site search for 'selective licensing' (322 results) and 'additional licensing' (795 results) returned no page describing any such scheme; all licensing hits were alcohol, animal, zoo, scrap metal or mandatory HMO. The HMO register page states only 'Certain HMOs are subject to mandatory HMO licensing'. No false-positive traps encountered: no Article 4 direction and no licensing consultation material was found on the housing pages.

notes: East Hampshire operates mandatory HMO licensing only. There is no selective licensing and no additional HMO licensing scheme. The council's 2026 price list contains HMO licence fees only, with no fee line for any discretionary scheme.
research: The HMO page states under 'Licensing of HMO's': 'It is a statutory requirement for us to operate a licensing scheme for HMOs with five or more people, from two or more households.' That is the national mandatory threshold, described expressly as a statutory duty rather than a local designation. FEE CORROBORATION: 'Prices for council services 2026' contains only these housing licence lines: HMO Licence (5 or less occupants) 5 year licence £600.00; 6 to 10 occupants £710.00; 11 to 15 £820.00; 16 to 20 £930.00; 20+ £1,040.00. There is no selective or additional licence fee anywhere in the schedule, which is strong corroboration because any live s.56 or Part 3 scheme must carry its own cost-recovery fee. COMMITTEE PAPERS: ModernGov document search for 'selective licensing' returned 1 result and 'additional licensing' returned 1 result, both the same Licensing Committee item of 11 September 2018, 'HMO Licensing Policy'. No designation report, statutory consultation or cabinet decision to designate. SITE STRUCTURE: the full sitemap contains no selective or additional licensing page; private sector housing subsections are limited to advice for renters, advice for tenants, disabled facilities grants, empty properties, HMO, private sector housing enforcement and mobile park homes. NOTE: the council's own site search returns an unfiltered generic list and is not usable for keyword confirmation, so the negative rests on the HMO page wording, the fee schedule, the sitemap and the ModernGov search.

notes: East Herts operates mandatory HMO licensing only, for properties with five or more occupants in two or more households. There is no selective or additional licensing. The environmental health fees list shows HMO licence fees only.
research: The HMO page is unusually explicit and effectively rules itself out: 'Not all HMOs require a licence. Currently, HMOs with 5 or more occupants in 2 or more households require a licence under the Housing Act 2004. In some other districts other properties also require a licence under additional or selective licensing.' The phrase 'in some OTHER districts' distinguishes East Herts from authorities that do operate such schemes. The same page repeats: 'Landlords currently need an HMO licence in most cases if a property has five or more occupants forming more than one household.' The HMO licence application page states 'Landlords need an HMO licence if a property has five or more tenants forming more than one household' with no mention of any discretionary scheme. FEE CORROBORATION: Environmental Health Fees and Charges lists only mandatory HMO lines - New: 'HMO licence with no more than five bedrooms - Part 1' £1,157, 'Part 2' £305, full fee on application £1,432, additional bedroom £31; Renewal: Part 1 £916, Part 2 £305, full fee £1,191, additional bedroom £31. No selective or additional licensing fee. LICENCE INDEX: the 'Licences and registration' index lists 17 licence types (alcohol, taxi, HMO, animal, food premises, betting, gaming machines, lotteries, skin piercing, sex establishments, charity collections, leaflet distribution, market traders, street trading, cooling towers, mobile homes site licences, scrap metal). HMO is the only private-rented-property licence. No Article 4 direction or licensing consultation was found.

notes: East Lindsey operates mandatory HMO licensing only. Its 2026-2029 HMO licensing policy states the council does not currently run an additional licensing scheme, and there is no selective licensing. The fee schedule lists mandatory HMO fees only.
research: The strongest negative in this batch because the council states it in writing. The South and East Lincolnshire Councils Partnership Housing Standards HMO Licensing Policy 2026-2029 says under its additional licensing heading: 'Under section 56 of the Housing Act 2004, additional licensing of HMOs covers those HMOs that are not licensed under the mandatory scheme but where the Council has used its power to designate areas of the Borough/District subject to additional licensing of HMOs. The Council do not currently operate an additional licensing scheme but maintain the right to introduce this if considered appropriate during the course of this policy.' The word 'selective' does not appear anywhere in the policy. The policy is partnership-wide, adopted across East Lindsey, South Holland and Boston. The HMO web page sets out the mandatory test only: the standard, self-contained flat or converted building test under s.254, 'The property is occupied by 5 or more people', and 'occupied by persons living in two or more separate households.' FEE CORROBORATION: the Enforcement Policy Fees and Charges appendix has a single housing licensing section headed 'HOUSES IN MULTIPLE OCCUPATION (HMO) LICENSING - Under Part 2 of the Housing Act 2004', with New Licence £300.00 initial application plus £150.00 for each unit of accommodation, renewal identical. No Part 3 selective fee and no s.56 additional fee. SITE SEARCH: council search for 'selective licensing' returns no results; 'additional licensing' returns only an unrelated large-music-event premises licence page.

notes: UNVERIFIED: East Riding's HMO page refers to an additional licensing scheme in Goole but gives no dates, and its April 2026 fee schedule lists mandatory HMO fees only. We could not confirm whether the Goole scheme is still in force. Check with the council.
research: DELIBERATELY NOT CONFIRMED EITHER WAY, because no live-or-expired verdict could be evidenced to a safe standard. The licensing page states: 'Under the national mandatory licensing scheme the definition of an HMO which must be licensed is one that has 5 or more people, forming 2 or more households, who are sharing facilities such as toilets, bathrooms and kitchens regardless of the number of storeys.' THE GOOLE REFERENCE: the only mention of any discretionary scheme sits inside a clearly historical section headed 'What are the changes to mandatory HMO licensing from 1 October 2018?', which reads: 'If you currently have an HMO licensed under the council's additional licensing scheme which operates in Goole and it falls under the new definition of a mandatory licensable HMO, your current licence will remain valid, and no action is needed until it comes up for renewal.' That paragraph is written in 2018 tense (surrounding text says 'New rules will also come into force') and is a transitional note, not a current designation statement. EVIDENCE IT IS NO LONGER LIVE: (1) the current fee schedule on the same page, expressly 'effective from 1 April 2026', lists only mandatory HMO fees - new 1-year £510.00 for a 5-bedroom property plus £25 per additional bedroom, new 5-year £1,205.00, renewal 1-year £510.00, renewal 5-year £1,015, pre-application advice £240 inc VAT, replacement licence £45 - with no additional or selective licensing fee line; (2) there is no application route or dedicated page for an additional licence, and probes of two plausible paths both returned 404; (3) the 'Available licences' index lists 'Houses in multiple occupation' as the only property licence; (4) a s.56 designation lasts a maximum of five years, so a scheme described as operating in 2018 would have lapsed by 2023 unless redesignated, and no redesignation is published. EVIDENCE AGAINST CALLING IT EXPIRED: the council's own live page still uses the present tense 'which operates in Goole', and no revocation notice, expiry date or committee decision could be found to date the end. NO SELECTIVE LICENSING FOUND: the A-Z has no selective licensing entry and the private housing landlords section covers only HMOs, landlord training, landlord liaison, HHSRS and general advice. LIMITS: the site search is JavaScript-rendered and could not be queried server-side, and the ModernGov committee site returned HTTP 522. A landlord in Goole with a 3-4 occupant HMO or a s.257 converted building could be misled either way, so this is flagged unverified rather than given a false negative. ACTION: confirm with private.sector.housing@eastriding.gov.uk or h.licensing@eastriding.gov.uk before relying on a nil return for a Goole property.

notes: East Suffolk operates mandatory HMO licensing only, for properties with five or more people in two or more households. There is no selective or additional licensing. The 2026/27 fees schedule lists HMO licence fees only.
research: The HMO page states: 'All HMOs with five or more people living in two or more households, regardless of the number of storeys in the property, need to be licensed. This includes any flat which contains five or more people living in two or more households where the flat has not been purpose-built to multiple occupant standards and flats above or below commercial premises.' Mandatory test only. The page also carries a stale pre-2018 line, 'Generally speaking, this will apply to any HMO of three or more storeys that is occupied by five or more people in two or more households', still mandatory wording. POTENTIAL FALSE POSITIVE: the page ends 'All HMOs (licensable or otherwise) should also be registered with the local council.' That is an administrative or voluntary registration statement with no fee and no designation behind it; it is NOT a s.56 or Part 3 scheme. FEE CORROBORATION: the fees and charges schedule 2026/27, Housing Services section 6.1, is headed 'Houses of multiple occupancy licences' and is the only housing licensing fee in the document: new licence up to and including seven lettable units, Part A £515.85 plus Part B £714.05, total £1,229.90, additional £25.00 per unit over seven; renewal Part A £345.81 plus Part B £702.72, total £1,048.53. Searching the whole schedule for 'selective' and 'additional licensing' returns zero matches. COMMITTEE PAPERS: CMIS search for 'selective licensing' returned 8 documents, none a designation. Cabinet 03/02/2026 hits are boilerplate statutory offence lists in the Private Sector Housing Enforcement and Civil Penalties Policy, which merely recite available powers. Overview and Scrutiny 18/09/2025 minutes contain one passing line and record 'The possibility of licensing landlords to drive up standards' as a discussion point, with no designation, consultation, dates or wards, so nothing meets the bar for 'proposed'. SITE STRUCTURE: the full sitemap contains no selective or additional licensing page.

notes: Eastbourne operates mandatory HMO licensing only. There is no selective or additional licensing. An Article 4 direction restricts HMO conversions in some wards, but that is planning control, not licensing, and no licence arises from it.
research: Council statement, last modified 23 July 2025, under the heading 'HMO Licensing': 'Eastbourne Borough Council currently operates a mandatory licensing scheme under the Housing Act 2004, which requires an HMO licence for any property with 5 or more unrelated occupiers living as separate households and sharing amenities.' The HMO licensing page covers application forms, prescribed standards, registers and fees, with no mention of additional licensing, selective licensing, designated areas or wards. FEE CORROBORATION: the 'HMO License Fee Schedule 2026-2027' contains categories only for Shared House (5, 6, 7, 8, 9+ persons), Bedsit (2-6+ bedsits) and Hostel, plus ancillary fees. It states 'As shared houses are licensed for 5 or more occupants...' and refers only to 'an application for a licence under Part 2 of the Housing Act 2004'. No selective or additional fee exists. COUNCIL'S OWN EVIDENCE BASE: the Eastbourne HMO Study 2024 (AECOM, February 2024), Executive Summary p.2, states 'No relevant Article 4 Directions or additional licensing schemes are in force. Eastbourne therefore has an opportunity to intervene...'. The study offered additional licensing only as an option; the council chose the planning route instead, so there is nothing at consultation stage to record as 'proposed'. COMMITTEE PAPERS: full-text search of the ModernGov archive returned 'No results found' for both 'selective licensing' and 'additional licensing', and none for 'section 56'. FALSE POSITIVE TRAPS: (1) two pages that look like scheme pages are generic ESD/LGA records-retention schedule entries published as boilerplate on many council sites, not evidence of a scheme. (2) An Article 4 Direction came into force 30 July 2025 withdrawing permitted development rights for C3 to C4 small HMO conversions in Devonshire, Meads and Upperton wards and part of St Anthonys ward, alongside an HMO Supplementary Planning Document adopted July 2025. Planning control, not licensing. (3) FOI 14362 confirming mandatory-only is a LEWES District Council response and must not be attributed to Eastbourne, although the two share one private housing team and one fee schedule.

notes: Eastleigh states it currently operates a mandatory HMO licensing scheme only. There is no selective licensing and no additional HMO licensing. The council's fees page lists mandatory HMO licence fees only.
research: The cleanest negative in this batch: the council itself sets out all three regimes and says which one it runs. Housing licences page: 'There are three different licensing regimes for housing: Mandatory licensing of large HMOs; Additional licensing (optional) for smaller HMOs in select areas; Selective licensing (optional) for other rented accommodation in select areas. We currently only operate a Mandatory Licensing Scheme.' The same page explains the national change effective 1 October 2018. FEE CORROBORATION: housing fees and charges from 1 October 2025 list 'HMO licensing - up to 5 occupants - £1,450 total split as £725 on application and £725 on the decision to grant' and 'over 5 occupants - £37.50 per additional occupant (up to a maximum of £1,600)'. Remaining lines are immigration inspection, health check visit and notice-service fees. No selective or additional licence fee line. COMMITTEE PAPERS: ModernGov search for 'selective licensing' returned 3 results, none a designation. Cabinet 22/01/2024 'Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO) Licensing and Fees Policy' states 'The Council has a statutory duty to administer the mandatory licensing regime in respect of Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs) which are to be occupied by five or more persons within the Borough.' The other two hits concern the Private Sector Housing Enforcement and Civil Penalties Policy under the Renters' Rights Act 2025, which is enforcement, not designation. 'additional licensing' returned 5 results, all gambling, taxi or licensing-administration items. FALSE POSITIVE TRAP: a news item of 28 February 2020, 'Private sector housing consultation', concerns a draft enforcement policy and civil penalties, NOT a licensing designation consultation. ACCESS NOTE: the domain sits behind a Cloudflare managed challenge that 403s plain fetches; content was read via a full browser session.

notes: Elmbridge operates mandatory HMO licensing only, for properties occupied by five or more people in two or more households. There is no selective or additional licensing, and only one HMO licence fee (£600) is published.
research: The HMO page states: 'A house in multiple occupation (HMO) is a property that is let to at least 3 unrelated tenants who form more than 1 household and who share a kitchen, bathroom, toilet or another room. All houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) occupied by 5 or more people who are not living together as a single household, but share facilities, need to be licensed.' Note the 3-tenant figure is the s.254 DEFINITION of an HMO, not the licensing trigger; the licensing trigger given is the mandatory 5-person threshold. The page contains no occurrence of 'selective' or 'additional licensing'. FEE CORROBORATION: same page, 'To apply for a 5-year HMO licence... pay the £600 application fee', plus a £50 discount for members of a recognised landlord association. Only one licence fee exists; there is no second fee line for any discretionary scheme, which a live s.56 or Part 3 designation would require. The landlord hub lists only MEES, HMOs, health and safety, damp and mould, and rent-a-room. SITE STRUCTURE: the complete sitemap (1,819 URLs) contains no URL matching 'selective' or 'additional licensing'. LIMITS: the site search is JavaScript-rendered and the ModernGov committee search requires a POST with viewstate, so keyword site-search and committee papers could not be checked directly. The negative rests on the HMO page wording, the single fee and complete sitemap enumeration, which is solid but marginally weaker than councils publishing an explicit 'mandatory only' statement.

notes: Epping Forest operates mandatory HMO licensing only, for HMOs with five or more occupants in two or more households. There is no selective or additional licensing. Only one HMO licence fee is published, £1,036 per five units.
research: The HMO pages state: 'A house in multiple occupation, known as a HMO, is a property occupied by 3 or more people (including children) who form more than 1 family and share either a kitchen or a bathroom... If the HMO has 5 or more occupants, living as 2 or more households, sharing facilities, it must be licensed.' And: 'A licence must be applied for before a property is occupied by 5 or more people, who share facilities and are unrelated.' Mandatory threshold only. FALSE POSITIVE TRAP: the same page states 'A property with more than 6 occupants must have planning permission to operate as a large HMO'. That is a planning requirement, a C4 to sui generis change of use, not licensing. FEE CORROBORATION: 'A licence fee per 5 units of accommodation is £1,036.00. An additional £41.00 is charged for each extra unit of accommodation.' A single mandatory fee with no discretionary scheme fee. Housing conditions and enforcement, and advice for landlords, show enforcement via HHSRS statutory notices only. SITE STRUCTURE: full sitemap sweep (588 page URLs, 312 news items) found no page or news item mentioning selective or additional licensing; the only other licensing page under private housing is park home and caravan site licensing. LIMITS: the site search is JavaScript-only and the ModernGov site returned HTTP 522, so committee papers could not be verified directly. The news sitemap contains no licensing-designation item.

notes: Epsom and Ewell operates mandatory HMO licensing only, for properties with five or more people in two or more households. There is no selective or additional licensing, and the online fee database lists HMO licence fees only.
research: The HMO page states: 'A HMO must have a licence if any of the following apply: It meets the definition of an HMO - It is occupied by five or more people forming at least two households'. Mandatory threshold only, with no mention of selective or additional licensing. FEE CORROBORATION, strong because it is a live queryable database rather than a static page: the council's fee database filtered to 'Houses of Multiple Occupation' returns exactly two lines, 'Application up to 5 units (or lets)' £833.00 per application or renewal, and 'Application over 5 units (or lets)' £173.00 per unit. No selective or additional licensing fee exists in the council's fee system. SITE SEARCH CORROBORATION: a search for 'selective licensing' returns 'Your search yielded no results'. A search for 'additional licensing' returns only irrelevant hits (Local Plan 'additional documents', taxi and pavement licensing). No Article 4 direction relating to HMOs and no licensing consultation were found.

schemes.areaDescription: A city-wide additional HMO licensing scheme covering two specific property types: flats or maisonettes above commercial premises or in mixed-use buildings let to 3 or more people in more than one household sharing amenities; and buildings converted into self-contained flats where the conversion did not meet the 1991 Building Regulations and fewer than two thirds of the flats are owner-occupied. The council states the scheme ran until February 2020 and has expired, and that no renewal is needed. It does not publish the designation start date or an exact end date, so both are recorded as null rather than estimated.

notes: Exeter's city-wide additional HMO licensing scheme has expired; the council says it ran until February 2020 and needs no renewal. Only mandatory HMO licensing now applies. An Article 4 direction controls HMO conversions, but that is planning, not licensing.
research: EXPIRED ADDITIONAL SCHEME, CONFIRMED IN THE COUNCIL'S OWN WORDS. The live application page states: 'our HMO additional licensing scheme has now expired. This form is for [Mandatory licensing only]' and 'The additional licensing scheme ran until February 2020. Your current additional licence will be valid for five years from the date of application. There is no requirement to apply for an additional licence renewal when your current licence expires.' The scheme is fully dead, with no successor designation and nothing at consultation stage. CURRENT REQUIREMENT: 'All HMOs with 5 or more occupiers living in 2 or more households' sharing amenities, plus 'Some flats, including those over shops, will also require a licence if they are occupied by 5 or more people, from 2 or more separate households', i.e. the national mandatory regime only. SCOPE OF THE FORMER SCHEME, from the council's own page as archived 18 August 2019: 'An Additional HMO Licensing Scheme covering specific types of HMO has been introduced throughout the city. The 2 types of HMO, which will need to be licensed are: flats or maisonettes either above commercial premises (shops, offices etc) or in mixed use buildings, where the flats or maisonettes are let to 3 or more people, forming more than one household, who share a kitchen, bathroom or toilet; buildings which have been converted into self contained flats, where the conversion does not meet the standards set by the 1991 Building Regulations, and where less than two thirds of the flats are owner occupied.' Coverage is therefore recorded as district ('throughout the city') rather than named wards. The designation start date is not published, and the end is given only as 'February 2020' with no day, so both are null rather than guessed. FEE CORROBORATION: the current 2025/2026 fee schedule has only mandatory HMO lines - Part A £298.70 with the application, Part B £772.50 base plus £10.80 per bedroom for bedrooms six and above, with a £125 reduction at Part B for accredited landlords. No additional licensing fee, confirming no live scheme. NO SELECTIVE LICENSING: council site search for 'selective licensing' returns 'No results found'. FALSE POSITIVE TRAP: Exeter has an HMO Supplementary Planning Document and an Article 4 Direction; the 2023 direction 'came into force on 23 December 2024' and covers 'part of Exeter', restricting permitted development rights to convert dwellings to HMOs. The council states plainly that 'Obtaining planning permission for an HMO and obtaining a licence for an HMO are separate processes.' Planning control with a commencement date and defined area, which must NOT be recorded as licensing.
